newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Silicon Valley Group raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Silicon Valley Group raised.

text.p: -- Morgan Stanley Jay Deanna said he raised his rating on Silicon Valley Group Inc to outperform from neutral.
-- The analyst said he set a target price of $22 per share. He had not previously had a target.
-- The analyst did not alter his earning projections.
-- Deanna said he is looking for strong growth in Silicon Valley Group's Micrascan product line when the company reports fiscal fourth quarter earnings Monday, October 28.
-- The analyst said he expected the company to ship 80 Micrascan units during fiscal 1997, up from his previous estimate of 55 to 60 units.

-- He said that he believed demand for deep-ultraviolet photolithography chipmaking systems was strengthening and that the company will see a strong increase in sequential bookings growth for the September quarter in its report Monday.

-- He said he based this expectation on conversations with customers and other industry sources and contrasted his bullish view with his earlier view -- based on talks with management in July -- that September bookings would fall below those seen in the June quarter, when 15 Micrascans shipped.

-- He said he expected to strong demand going-forward for deep-UV ultraviolet equipment, due in part to the addition of Motorola Inc as a volume customer for Micrascan, in addition to existing customers Intel Corp and International Business Machines Corp.
-- The analyst said he would alter his earnings estimates after the company reports fiscal 1996 year earnings Monday.

-- "We think our (profit) margin estimates estimates may be too high for the next few quarter, but we think our fiscal 1997 revenue estimates for Microscan, Track and Thermco are too low," the analyst wrote.
-- He said Microscan, its main Deep UV product, accounted for roughly 35 percent of SGVI's business in the June quarter, while Track and Thermco collective produced about 64 percent.
-- The stock was up 1-1/8 to 17-1/8 by mid-morning Friday.
